about: Claims about kmerseek, each tied to rows of data/experiments.json. Every number shown with a claim is looked up from that file by row id and number name, so it is never typed twice. Written 2026-09-29.

claims.name: Short features placed
claims.statement: kmerseek places short protein features (under 60 amino acids) on the matching stretch of a closely related protein, and its call stops where the feature stops. On most of these features, Foldseek's call runs past the feature.

evidence.name: cases_passing_every_criterion
evidence.say: short features where kmerseek draws the boundary and every other tool's call runs past it

evidence.name: foldseek_spills_on_223_rows
evidence.say: of 223 short features kmerseek placed, the number where Foldseek's call ran past the feature

evidence.name: hero_kmerseek_call
evidence.say: COL9A1 Collagen-like 7 in chicken: kmerseek's call

evidence.name: hero_foldseek_call_iou
evidence.say: the same feature: Foldseek's call

evidence.name: exact_beats_best_tool_cases
evidence.say: of the 87 cases, where exact seeds still beat the best other tool after a rebuild

evidence.name: cases_extension_keeps_iou_within_0.05
evidence.say: cases where growing the seed outward keeps the boundary; so this claim is about exact seeds only

evidence.name: kmerseek arms above a Kyte-Doolittle scan (no search) on all features
evidence.say: across all Swiss-Prot features, not only the short ones, a hydrophobicity scan with no database beats every kmerseek setting

claims.caveats: The comparison tools do not include a per-family Pfam search (hmmscan), which draws one box per domain unit. That is the first test a reviewer will ask for, and it has not been run.

claims.name: Short Pfam domain boundaries
claims.statement: For Pfam domains that are a small part of their protein, kmerseek draws the domain boundary more often than structure search, and less often than phmmer and MMseqs2.

claims.caveats: Notebook 238 is a pilot on the 255 MHC-region queries. The full run is pull request 75.

claims.name: H/P pattern kept in homologs
claims.statement: Homologous proteins keep their hydrophobic/polar pattern at 20 to 30% identity, well above chance. BLOSUM62 predicts nearly the same share of class-keeping substitutions, so this is not specific to the 2-letter alphabet.

evidence.name: hp_thomas_dill2 kappa, Pfam seed pairs at 20-30% identity
evidence.say: agreement of the H/P class at aligned positions, Cohen's kappa (0 = chance, 1 = always the same)

evidence.name: protein20 kappa, Pfam seed pairs at 20-30% identity
evidence.say: the same for the 20-letter alphabet

evidence.name: observed share of substitutions keeping the Thomas-Dill class, 20-30%
evidence.say: share of substitutions that keep the H/P class

evidence.name: BLOSUM62 expectation for the same
evidence.say: what BLOSUM62 predicts for that share

claims.name: Remote homologs
claims.statement: On remote homologs, kmerseek stops placing labels at a higher identity than Foldseek and phmmer. The H/P pattern is kept, but in runs too short for an exact seed to stand out from chance.

evidence.name: share of Pfam 20-30% pairs sharing an exact hp_thomas_dill2 23-mer (column 23)
evidence.say: remote homolog pairs that share even one exact 23-letter H/P seed

evidence.name: globin_lowest_identity_correct_kmerseek_best_of_150
evidence.say: globins: lowest identity (%) at which kmerseek's best of 150 settings still places the label

evidence.name: globin_lowest_identity_correct_foldseek
evidence.say: the same, Foldseek

evidence.name: globin_lowest_identity_correct_phmmer
evidence.say: the same, phmmer

evidence.say: Ced9 against human: share of random human proteins that rank as well as BCL2 or better

evidence.name: bcl2_best_evalue_bits_short_of_e1
evidence.say: BCL2's best measured E-value, in bits short of E = 1

evidence.name: pairs with a region / at E <= 0.01 / at E <= 0.1
evidence.say: cross-family SCOPe pairs under 20% identity found by the real kmerseek search at E ≤ 0.01

evidence.name: crossover divergence vs phmmer
evidence.say: species distance from human beyond which kmerseek transfers Pfam domains worse than phmmer

claims.caveats: kmerseek's lowest identity is its best of 150 settings, picked after seeing the results. The distance where phmmer overtakes kmerseek (notebook 236) depends on how duplicate transfers are counted; a project note records about 166 Mya on the duplicate-removed tables, against the 108 Mya printed in notebook 236.

claims.statement: A short seed grown outward while the H/P classes mostly agree reaches remote homologs in a test on aligned pairs, but not yet in a real database search, and growing the seed loses the tight boundary on short features.

evidence.say: boundary overlap on the 87 short features, exact seeds against grown seeds

claims.name: SCOPe40 against Foldseek
claims.statement: kmerseek does not beat Foldseek on the SCOPe40 structural benchmark. Earlier wins came from scoring only the queries where kmerseek made a call, and from counting a same-family hit as a superfamily hit.

claims.name: ELM motifs
claims.statement: kmerseek does not place short linear motifs (ELM, 3 to 15 amino acids) that other tools miss, and it puts fewer motifs at the right position than jackhmmer.

evidence.name: motifs_only_kmerseek_places
evidence.say: chicken: motifs kmerseek places on the ortholog and no other tool does

evidence.name: kmerseek_best_arm_on_position_share
evidence.say: chicken: share of motifs put on position, kmerseek's best setting

evidence.name: jackhmmer_on_position_share
evidence.say: the same, jackhmmer

evidence.name: share_run_ge_19_ciona
evidence.say: Ciona: motifs whose flanks keep a 19-letter H/P run, the length an exact seed needs

claims.caveats: Chicken only. The seven farther species are pull request 72, not run yet.

claims.name: Ranking score
claims.statement: kmerseek's per-region score region_mean_idf rises with the length of the call, so a list sorted by it tends to put long calls first.

evidence.name: spearman_region_mean_idf_vs_call_length_median
evidence.say: rank correlation of region_mean_idf with call length, median over 266 settings (ELM, chicken)

evidence.name: spearman_mean_idf_vs_call_length_median
evidence.say: the same on DisProt regions

evidence.name: heldout_average_precision_all_19_alphabets
evidence.say: a model trained on all 19 alphabets' scores: held-out average precision

evidence.name: bcl2_combined_rank_mean_idf
evidence.say: BCL2's rank for Ced9 after combining alphabets

claims.caveats: Pull request 71 changes the cut to keep a target if either region_mean_idf or region_evalue ranks it in the top 1,000.

claims.name: BHF
claims.statement: kmerseek has not found a human protein that matches BHF better than chance, and BHF is not among the Botryllus proteins that human MHC queries hit.

evidence.name: bhf_best_evalue_any_human_protein
evidence.say: BHF against the human proteome: the best E-value over 152 settings. E = 1 means one hit this good is expected by chance in a single search, so the best of 152 searches falling below 1 is expected too

evidence.name: BHF among the hits
evidence.say: BHF among the Botryllus proteins that human MHC queries hit

claims.caveats: BHF's membrane localization is a lab measurement and does not rest on kmerseek.

claims.name: Cost and memory
claims.statement: Among the tools notebook 227 timed, kmerseek uses the fewest CPU-hours per proteome search. A Swiss-Prot-sized search needs far more memory than MMseqs2 or DIAMOND and answers fewer queries per second.

claims.statement: kmerseek labels proteins in an invertebrate proteome (Botryllus) that sequence search leaves without a label, and the labels beat a shuffled-sequence control.
